newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia prepares to open Sept coffee registration.
newsitem.headline: Colombia prepares to open Sept coffee registration.

text.p: Colombia will open registrations for September coffee exports next week once all August export commitments are fulfilled, the head of the National Coffee Growers' Federation said on Monday.

Coffee czar Jorge Cardenas also said Colombia would maintain its 30 U.S. cent quality premium on its international sales, contradicting market rumours that the premium could be cut to 20 cents to make the Colombian beans more competitive.
"Registrations for September will open next week once we have closed our August positions," Cardenas told reporters after the weekly federation meeting.

"What is clear is that when we open registrations we will retain the 30 cent premium because we have the confidence that the market is on the way to stabilising and even strengthening," he said. "The idea is to take the risk and maintain the premium."

Colombian arabica is seen as one of the best quality coffees in the world and the federation adds the 30 cent premium to the average trading price of Central American coffees in the previous three days in order to obtain what it believes is a fair reward for the good quality.
Cardenas did not specify what day next week the September registrations could be opened.
Colombia is on target to produce just under 10 million 60-kg bags of coffee in the 1996-97 cycle which ends before the start of the main harvest in September.

In order to meet this year's export schedule the federation has had to dip heavily into its inventories. Cardenas said those stocks now stood at 4.5 million bags compared to about 6.4 million bags at the same time last year.
He did not comment on how much of those stocks were fresh and how much was old coffee.
